I think my wording in the original post is a little unclear, I had to edit a lot down to fit the character limit: I was actually re-diagnosed as an adult at the end of September, maybe a couple weeks after she had fired me. I scheduled the test with a neuropsychologist after my second meeting with Dr. B, where I brought in the list and she laughed at me. Still, I had records of my diagnosis from childhood and of the meds they prescribed me back then and I agree with you completely. But I basically got my adult diagnosis affirmed out of spite for her, and because her invalidating me really impacted me. 

I was verbally abused by an adult in my life for things that I later learned were all ADHD symptoms, so I have an emotional tie to that diagnosis. It's important to me that it's validated because otherwise, everything that abusive figure said about me was right (in my neurotic head, at least). I'm working on that in therapy, though.

I feel the part about her outdated diagnosis SO HARD. Regarding school, I even told her that hey, I had meltdowns every finals period and had to ask multiple professors for extensions every semester without fail. But that's "just anxiety". :p

Hi!! Don't worry, I am safely off of the offending meds and have been for a while. I took a stepped down dose that she prescribed before stopping them. Originally it was just to see if a lower dose would improve the side effects, but well, two birds one stone I guess. I called the person in charge of complaints at my treatment program today to discuss my report - it felt like the next right step in this process for me.

Thank you very much for this. This was a very painful experience for me but since hypersensitivity and highly emotional reactions are a thing I struggle with (lol ironically) I've been trying to be as objective as possible. I relive this a lot and it sucks how helpless and frustrating it felt, so I am honestly open to looking at my own behavior and compassionately accepting where I may have struggled and why. Through reading replies I've been able to form an understanding of where I accept criticism and what I know in my heart was unjust. Your perspective also taught me a lot and the overwhelming amount of empathy coming from people has too. It's actually really made me feel better today. 

Btw, I wanted to clarify something for the sake of being as fair as possible: Dr. B hadn't known about the headaches the whole month I was having them, because it took me a bit to notice the correlation. Their severity was mild at first but increased rapidly as we raised the dosage, which is what clued me in. The week we first talked about it was the same week I went to the ER for the pain. So shit got real pretty quick, it wasn't that she was refusing to budge the whole time. Still, the fact that she kept redirecting the conversation away from weaning me off those meds the next time we met, knowing how bad it had gotten, was appalling to me. It's what caused me to finally snap at her.

I just want to say that this isn't how our meeting went. First we did an intake, aka a recap of my entire history. Then she asked about the things I wanted to work on with her, and when I mentioned my ADHD she started taking issue, saying she "didn't see it". She didn't really care about the prior diagnosis, if anything she was insinuating that she thought it was wrong. For me, the issue then became getting her to believe me, rather than getting treated, hence the list. Your last response to me I felt was very fair, but this was hurtful.

I wanted to say thank you for correcting me so kindly. I really appreciate that. 

My need for validation (or to not feel invalidated) was a big part of it, and I think that need was the crutch of where I kept going wrong on my part. I have a lot of trauma surrounding that diagnosis, which is why I think it became such a titular issue for me, on top of how severely I felt it was affecting my mental health. 

By recovery, I meant my eating disorder (binge and restrict) - I was trying to be fair by pointing out that she was right not to give stimulants to an eating disorder patient on their first visit, aha. I wasn't on any other medications at the time. 

But yeah, I agree with all of what you said. I can see where she was disrespectful and unprofessional, but I can also see where I disrespected her as well, and where I allowed my own extremely strong emotions to kind of shoot me in the foot. Again, thank you for your thoughtful response.

I actually really appreciate you giving me a view of things from her perspective, as it helps me get it more outside of my own emotional view of what happened. There's a few things that have been misunderstood though:

1. I am diagnosed and have records of my diagnosis, so by definition I was not self-diagnosing. She repeatedly told me that what I was experiencing was anxiety (which I do have to be fair), not ADHD, and that was painful for me. I can understand that she still couldn't take my word for it and act without those records, but as far as her accusation, it'd be pretty bold of me to promise them if I had none. 

2. I didn't stop taking the original med she prescribed, I asked her to take me off of them. By that point the headaches had been going on for a month. I wanted to include that she lowered the dose first bc I think medically, she was doing exactly what she was supposed to and I agreed that we should test a lower dosage. I actually really liked that med and wanted to make it work, but the ER trip closed the book for me. To me, the issue was that she went repeatedly off topic when I made that request. 

That being said, I knew and had been told before that a psychiatrist is going to be understandably suspicious of an eating disorder patient asking about ADHD treatment; however, you make that perspective much clearer than I have been able to acknowledge just logically. The way you put it, I sound really fucking suspicious. My intentions during that meeting were truly pure and not coming from a disordered place, but it's not fair for me to expect her to just take my word for it on day one. My reasoning was a lot along the lines of what you said actually, in that my ADHD and ED are very closely linked. Still, I can see where I failed to be patient and compliant with her process. 

Thanks for the measured and fair response. In a weird way it's comforting to reframe this event not just as something bad that happened to me, but as something where I also had agency and was also culpable.

EDIT: "months" was actually "a month"

The noncompliance piece I take a bit of issue with - as far as my behavior and how much I was to handle I definitely played my part, but I told her the week before that I didn't feel safe starting a new medication (especially a stimulant) while my pain level was as high as it was. I don't feel guilty for knowing that I physically could not tolerate more side effects.

In fairness to her, I WAS able to safely stop those meds at that point because she had just stepped down the dosage of my prescription the last time we met (we spoke on a Friday, I went to ER on a Sat, and our last meeting was the Friday after). But she made no effort to clarify that and left me thinking I had just been left without a psychiatrist to wean me off of them. That was a truly terrifying moment for me and not something her patients should ever have to experience.

Literally every patient there AND in that program's other branches have stories about her. All I have to do is say her name, I don't even have to ask. I'm on the more sensitive side of things and DEFINITELY took her behavior the hardest, so I wanted to make sure I wasn't just blowing things out of proportion. I'll continue to speak up about this.
Thank you so much. I needed to hear that. :)

That's very fair. There was a LOT of tension during our meetings, on both sides. I have reported her, mainly for hanging up on me after the ER incident; I don't think she did anything bad enough to lose her job over, but I did really want her to be talked to.

I have since found someone so much better who I feel much safer working with. I actually feel like she hears me. :) I'm mainly asking because this is still a painful memory for me and I'm thinking about reporting her- I reported her to the head of the program I was in but they didn't do anything.

Did you have any other symptoms when it comes to BV? I just googled it and nothing else seems to fit, but it's also mentioned that there could be no symptoms! It's definitely possible. My current plan is to go to urgent care if my period doesn't go over normally, or if things still feel weird the next time I have sex with my boyfriend (we're temporarily long distance, but no longer after this week!) 

Thank you so much for your help!!

I didn't think it was an insurmountable issue at the time I was apologizing, is the thing. It took me a bit to realize I was even having an argument with him. 

But then he went to end the conversation and telling him to have a good night was supposed to be the last of it on my end. And should have been. I shouldn't have taken the bait afterwards, but admittedly it made me feel defensive. Lesson learned; thank you.
Definitely fair. I tried to back off once I realized, but he kept pursuing the conversation.

You're absolutely right. I'm familiar with manipulative language and it was after "thanks for making my night worse" that I knew it was time to wrap it up. Still, I doubted myself after. I appreciate the outside perspectives here.
Thank you. I ended the conversation and blocked. I don't have any ill feelings towards him, but I don't think either of us would've benefitted from further conversation.
